bottomLine: Entitled sites are the leverage. With NIC MAP occupancy at 90.4% and starts near a 14-year low, operators are short on approved pads, so ATCO leads every conversation with entitlement in hand and keeps its economics in development, construction and co-GP equity.

partners.name: Benchmark Senior Living + National Development
partners.role: Operator and co-GP on rental AL/MC pads
partners.footprint: 68 Northeast communities; 21 in CT (9 in Fairfield County). Mount Pleasant NY opened 2025; Scotch Plains NJ (86 units) opening fall 2026; East Islip NY (90 units) closed a $41.1M construction loan in July 2026; Newtown CT acquired.
partners.structure: Development JV: National Development capital plus a Benchmark affiliate; Benchmark manages
partners.signal: Building now, with bank construction debt available to them in 2026. Already the named operator at Cortlandt (Evergreen Manor).

partners.name: Engel Burman (The Bristal)
partners.role: Operator-developer for the AL/MC pad inside an age-restricted plan
partners.footprint: 23 Bristal communities across Long Island, Westchester (White Plains, Armonk), Manhattan and North NJ (Englewood, Woodcliff Lake, Paramus).
partners.structure: Owner-operator with Harrison Street and Northwinds capital; builds in-house
partners.signal: Mid-90s occupancy; their configuration is exactly Florham Park and Montville.

partners.name: Sunrise Senior Living
partners.role: Manager or JV partner on luxury AL/MC; buyer of entitled sites
partners.footprint: 230+ communities. NY metro: The Apsley (UWS), Battery Park, Bridgewater and Franklin Lakes NJ; contract vendee at 900 King St, Rye Brook.
partners.signal: BDT & MSD buying a majority stake (Oct 6, 2026); 50+ community pipeline with 6–7 starts planned next year, Tarrytown NY named.

partners.name: LCS (Life Care Services / LCS Development)
partners.footprint: 139 communities in 30+ states; Broadview at Purchase College (Westchester).
partners.structure: Fee development and management for nonprofit or institutional owners
partners.signal: Broadview was 60% presold before construction and 90%+ reserved at opening. Closest for-profit template to RiverSpring.

bench.name: Epoch Senior Living
bench.note: Memory care in CT (Bridges at Trumbull and Norwalk; Rivermere launched Aug 2026). First call for Trumbull's MC wing.

bench.name: Brightview (Shelter Group)
bench.note: 19 tri-state communities, 4 in development; 94% occupancy on assets recapped with Harrison Street. Buyer of entitled pads or co-GP.

bench.name: Juniper Communities
bench.note: Middle-market NJ operator managing for NHI (Paramus). Fallback for Montville or Poughkeepsie.

bench.name: The Arbor Company
bench.note: Runs developer-capital JVs, the same structure ATCO would use, and is now competing supply at Florham Park.

bench.name: Atria
bench.note: Manages IL-heavy product for Ventas, including a community next to 900 King St. Competitor, not a lead.

sponsors.name: The Osborn (Rye, NY)
sponsors.note: 55.8-acre nonprofit CCRC next to Rye Brook whose campus expansion stalled on neighbor opposition. An approved off-campus site could solve that (our inference; untested).

sponsors.name: Kendal
sponsors.note: Quaker nonprofit system that grows by affiliation (11 affiliates in 7 states); Kendal on Hudson in Sleepy Hollow.

sponsors.name: Springpoint Senior Living
sponsors.note: NJ nonprofit, 8 communities; $114.8M of tax-exempt bonds via Ziegler. The natural NJ entrance-fee sponsor.

NJ-04.why: Their look-alike CCRC model matches a 114-unit AL/MC pad inside a 305-unit age-restricted plan.
NJ-04.watch: Arbor Terrace Florham Park (80 AL/MC units, Braemar + GEM JV) started construction Oct 13, 2026 and opens late 2027 in the same submarket. Re-test absorption and rents before LOI.

NJ-06.why: Their Scotch Plains NJ deal (86 AL/MC units) is the template for this pad.
NJ-06.watch: Same Arbor Terrace overlap as Florham Park. Pick Florham Park or Whippany unless demand supports both.

NJ-10.why: AL/MC pad next to 266 approved age-restricted homes, the Bristal configuration.
NJ-10.watch: Erickson's Cedar Crest (Pompton Plains) and Brightview Wayne draw on the same 75+ base.

NY-10.second: Juniper or a regional middle-market operator
NY-10.why: Middle-market rents fit their suburban format (our inference).
NY-10.watch: Thinner operator bench in Dutchess. Ask EFG/Saber who they have already spoken to.

NY-03.why: The applicant's attorney told the Planning Board on Feb 3, 2026 that Benchmark wants a 100-unit, 118-bed AL here.
NY-03.watch: ATCO's role is capital or GC alongside VS Construction and Benchmark. For an ATCO-controlled deal in the district, use NY-04 and pitch Sunrise or Brightview.

CT-02.why: Epoch is expanding CT memory care and already runs Bridges at Trumbull.
CT-02.watch: The owner said in 2023 he would sell or joint-venture with an operator.

NY-01.why: Sunrise controls the site; offer ATCO as GC or fee developer.
NY-01.watch: For-profit the deal loses about $7.9M; nonprofit-sponsored it makes about $26M with a $6.7M ATCO fee. ATCO's money is in fees and construction, not ownership.

structures.t: Management contract on an ATCO-owned asset
structures.econ: Keep 90–100% of equity; pay about 5% of revenue plus an incentive fee (industry norm)
structures.when: Where ATCO wants the long-term hold and a lender-approved operator

structures.t: Development JV with an operator affiliate
structures.econ: ATCO as developer/GC and co-GP; operator co-invests 5–10% (inferred); institutional LP equity
structures.when: The default for the NJ and NY pads

structures.t: Sale or ground lease of an entitled pad
structures.econ: Land profit plus the GC contract where negotiable
structures.when: Where the operator insists on control

structures.t: Fee development for a nonprofit sponsor
structures.who: LCS + Purchase College; ID2 at River's Edge
structures.econ: Development fee of about 4–5% of cost, plus GC and possibly ground rent
structures.when: Rye Brook and any institutional land; tax-exempt bonds need a 501(c)(3) borrower

next: Benchmark / National Development: pitch Whippany and Poughkeepsie as a two-site program; ask about Cortlandt and an ATCO capital or GC role.
Engel Burman: pitch Florham Park and Montville as look-alike CCRC pads with the age-restricted builders already approved.
Sunrise: open Rye Brook (GC or fee-development role) and their Westchester pipeline under the new BDT & MSD capital.
LCS + The Osborn: test a nonprofit entrance-fee Rye Brook as the fallback if Sunrise does not close.
Epoch: the memory-care component at Trumbull.
Before any Morris County LOI, re-run absorption with Arbor Terrace Florham Park in the supply set.
